Key Finding: Unequal internet access can exclude people from a Web or Android service, especially in low-income and rural populations.
APA Reference: International Telecommunication Union. (2024). Measuring digital development: Facts and figures 2024. https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/facts-figures-2024/

Key Finding: About one billion people live with disabilities, so inaccessible interfaces can systematically exclude a large user population.
APA Reference: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs. (n.d.). Factsheet on persons with disabilities. https://www.un.org/development/desa/disabilities/resources/factsheet-on-persons-with-disabilities.html

Key Finding: The digital divide includes affordability and gender gaps, not only network coverage, so adoption strategies must address both access and participation.
APA Reference: International Telecommunication Union. (2023). Measuring digital development: Facts and figures 2023. https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/facts-figures-2023/

Key Finding: Federated sign-in can reduce password burden, but identity, session, and account-linking decisions remain security-critical implementation concerns.
APA Reference: Google. (n.d.). Integrate Credential Manager with Sign in with Google. https://developer.android.com/training/sign-in/credential-manager

Key Finding: Authentication guidelines increasingly support phishing-resistant, passkey, and synchronized credential options alongside traditional federated identity.
APA Reference: National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2024). SP 800-63B-4: Digital identity guidelines. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-63B-4

Key Finding: Broken access control and authorization failures remain major application risks, making role and resource boundaries central to secure MVP design.
APA Reference: OWASP Foundation. (2021). OWASP Top 10:2021. https://owasp.org/Top10/

Key Finding: Mobile and Web delivery can reduce distribution costs, but payment, device, connectivity, and support costs determine whether users can participate.
APA Reference: International Telecommunication Union. (2024). Measuring digital development: Facts and figures 2024. https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/facts-figures-2024/

Key Finding: Privacy and security incidents can impose direct response costs and can erode user trust, raising the value of prevention and incident readiness.
APA Reference: National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2020). NIST privacy framework: A tool for improving privacy through enterprise risk management. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.CSWP.01162020

Key Finding: Rapid digital growth may concentrate infrastructure and computing expenses in cloud providers, making usage forecasting and cost controls important.
APA Reference: International Energy Agency. (2025). Energy and AI. https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai

Key Finding: Cloud and data-centre electricity demand is projected to rise as digital and AI workloads expand, creating energy and emissions consequences.
APA Reference: International Energy Agency. (2025). Energy and AI. https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai

Key Finding: Global electronic waste reached 62 million tonnes in 2022 and was rising faster than documented recycling, reinforcing device longevity and e-waste concerns.
APA Reference: Baldé, C. P., et al. (2024). The global e-waste monitor 2024. https://ewastemonitor.info/the-global-e-waste-monitor-2024/

Key Finding: A privacy-preserving app should minimize unnecessary data and compute because each avoided transfer or retained record reduces resource demand.
APA Reference: United Nations. (n.d.). Sustainable consumption and production. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal12

Key Finding: Public digital policy increasingly links infrastructure, affordability, inclusion, and institutional trust, which can shape users' willingness to adopt a service.
APA Reference: International Telecommunication Union. (2024). Measuring digital development: Facts and figures 2024. https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/facts-figures-2024/

Key Finding: Cross-border digital regulation may change how services collect, transfer, store, and delete personal information, creating jurisdictional compliance risk.
APA Reference: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. (2013). OECD guidelines on the protection of privacy and transborder flows of personal data. https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264196391-en

Key Finding: Public disability policies and accessibility expectations may require inclusive interfaces and equivalent access across supported platforms.
APA Reference: United Nations. (2006). Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. https://www.ohchr.org/en/instruments/conventions/convention-rights-persons-disabilities

Key Finding: The Philippine Data Privacy Act requires lawful processing, personal-information protection, security, and appropriate rights for data subjects.
APA Reference: Republic Act No. 10173, Data Privacy Act of 2012. (2012). Official Gazette. https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10173_2012.html

Key Finding: Location protection and aggregation thresholds require explicit design choices because precise location and small groups can reveal individuals even after removal of names.
APA Reference: National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2020). NIST privacy framework. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.CSWP.01162020

Key Finding: Consent, purpose limitation, and data-subject rights become important when applications contemplate reuse or resale of personal or location-derived data.
APA Reference: European Parliament and Council. (2016). Regulation (EU) 2016/679. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj

Key Finding: Privacy-preserving design should minimize collection and avoid creating per-user trails because secondary use can cause harm even without malicious intent.
APA Reference: National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2020). NIST privacy framework. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.CSWP.01162020

Key Finding: Data resale or secondary use is ethically risky when users cannot foresee the use, control disclosure, or understand downstream effects.
APA Reference: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. (2013). OECD privacy guidelines. https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264196391-en

Key Finding: Small-group reporting can expose identities or sensitive patterns despite anonymization, so aggregation and suppression should be treated as privacy safeguards.
APA Reference: Garfinkel, S. (2015). De-identification of personal information (NIST IR 8053). https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.IR.8053
